setup.backup.text: The backup is encrypted; this computer cannot read it. Put it on another disk or a network drive - not only on this computer.
setup.backup.title: Save the backup
setup.blocked: The setup cannot be skipped. It takes only a few steps.
setup.choose: Pick one of the two ways. There is no default.
setup.confirm: I understand that this cannot be changed later
setup.done.text: The device is set up. From here you work in the overview.
setup.done.title: Done
setup.final: This choice applies to this profile and cannot be changed. Changing your mind later means creating a new profile and signing in again at every service.
setup.intro: One question has to be answered first. It cannot be changed later. Take your time.
setup.mirrored.cost: In return, your master secret is created once outside the secure chip during setup. In that single moment, malware on your computer could read it. Never again afterwards.
setup.mirrored.text: You can set up a second stick later that does everything this one does. Lose one and you use the other, and you get back into everything.
setup.mirrored.title: Yes, a spare is possible
setup.only.cost: In return there is no spare. If the stick is lost or breaks, you cannot get into the accounts you created with it – you would start over at every service.
setup.only.text: Everything stays inside the secure chip for good. No secret ever leaves it, at any point.
setup.only.title: No, this stick only
setup.pin.rule: At least six characters. Not your date of birth.
setup.pin.text: The PIN opens the device. Without it, it hands out nothing.
setup.pin.title: Set a PIN
setup.question: Should a spare key be possible later?
setup.recommend: For everyday use: allow a spare. Losing your only stick otherwise means losing every account. For a crypto wallet you can add a second profile without a spare later.
setup.recommend.title: Recommendation
setup.sheet.text: The sheet says what to do when both devices are gone. Print it, fill in the open lines by hand and keep it apart from the devices.
setup.sheet.title: Print the emergency sheet
setup.title: Before you start
sheet.file.text: An encrypted file. It can set up a new device. Write down by hand where it is:
sheet.file.title: 1. The backup file
sheet.intro: This sheet helps when no device is left. Without it, the accounts made with it are lost.
sheet.keep: Do not keep it next to the device. A sheet in the desk beside the device protects against nothing.
sheet.nopin: The PIN is deliberately not on this sheet.
sheet.only.warn: Careful: this device runs as "this device only". What is in the secure chip never leaves it and therefore does not come back with this backup either. If the device is gone, every service has to be started over.
sheet.pass.text: At least twelve characters; the device suggests eight words. The passphrase is deliberately not printed here - write it by hand and keep the sheet safe.
sheet.pass.title: 2. The passphrase of the backup
sheet.shares.text: The passphrase can be split into several parts, of which a few are enough. Who holds which envelope belongs here. A single envelope reveals nothing.
sheet.shares.title: 3. The envelopes (if made)
sheet.steps.text: Get a new device, open this program, load the backup file and enter the passphrase - or gather the needed envelopes. The entries are then back.
sheet.steps.title: 4. What to do in an emergency
socket.ask: The program %s wants to read the secret "%s". Allow? [y/N]
socket.claim: The name of the program comes from the operating system. It stays a name - not proof of who is behind it.
